ety.text: 16th century, from Latin obvius (“being in the way so as to meet, meeting, easy to access, at hand, ready, obvious”) + -ous, from ob- (“before”) + via (“way”).

parts: la:obvius<t:being in the way so as to meet, meeting, easy to access, at hand, ready, obvious>

senses.d: Easily discovered, seen, or understood; self-explanatory.

ety.text: Latin obviuslbor. Portuguese óbvio Learned borrowing from Latin obvius.

senses.d: In an obvious or clearly apparent manner.
ex: She was in floods of tears and obviously very upset.
She'd obviously not gone to sleep yet: her eyes were bloodshot with sleepiness.

senses.d: Used as a filler word, or to introduce information even when not obvious.
ex: You weren't to know, but I've spoken to, obviously, Jim about this, and ...

grp.label: in an obvious manner; clearly apparent
